## Question 1 (Data Frames)

|planet |moons|has_rings|
|-------|-----|---------|
|Earth  |1    |FALSE    |
|Mars   |2    |FALSE    |
|Jupiter|97   |TRUE     |
|Saturn |274  |TRUE     |

a) Create three vectors from the columns of the table above and combine them into a tibble named `planets`. Print the tibble.

b) Look at the short type abbreviation printed under each column name. Report what type R gave each of the three columns, and explain in a sentence or two why it is useful that a tibble keeps track of the type of each column.


## Question 2 (Data Files)

a) Download the [`factbook.csv`](../../data/factbook.csv){download="factbook.csv"} file and read it into R as a tibble. Tell R that any cell containing an asterisk (`*`) is actually missing.

b) Use a function from the easystats package to describe the distribution of all continuous variables in this tibble. Which variables contain missing values, and what is the mean of the `maternal_mortality` variable?


## Question 3 (Data Exploration)

Read the "factbook.csv" file into R again for this question (remembering to treat asterisks as missing) so that it can be answered on its own.

a) Use `qplot()` to plot the distribution/variation of the `birth_rate` variable. Which values are the most common for this variable?

b) Use `qplot()` to visualize the covariation of the `life_exp` and `net_migration_rate` variables. Do any points seem unusual on one or both variables?
